marking_schemes.question_text:
The element with highest ionization potential, is:
A. Hydrogen
B. Caesium
C. Radon
D. Helium
marking_schemes.scheme_text: D or Helium or He
key_points: Helium has the highest ionization potential among all elements
common_errors: Choosing Hydrogen due to confusion with smallest atom
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most candidates answered correctly. Some got confused with Hydrogen.
marking_schemes.topic: Periodic Properties and Variations of Properties

marking_schemes.question_text:
The inert electrode used in the electrolysis of acidified water, is:
A. Nickel
B. Platinum
C. Copper
D. Silver
marking_schemes.scheme_text: B or Platinum or Pt
key_points: Platinum is an inert electrode used in electrolysis of acidified water
common_errors: Choosing Nickel as the inert electrode
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Answered correctly by most candidates. A few candidates chose Nickel.

marking_schemes.question_text:
A compound with low boiling point, is:
A. Sodium chloride
B. Calcium chloride
C. Potassium chloride
D. Carbon tetrachloride
marking_schemes.scheme_text: D or Carbon tetra chloride or CCl4
key_points: Carbon tetrachloride is a covalent compound with low boiling point unlike ionic compounds NaCl, CaCl2, KCl
common_errors: Choosing NaCl due to lack of knowledge that CCl4 is a covalent compound
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Some candidates chose incorrect option NaCl as they had no idea that CCl4 is a covalent compound.

marking_schemes.question_text:
The acid which can produce carbon from cane sugar, is:
A. Concentrated Hydrochloric acid
B. Concentrated Nitric acid
C. Concentrated Sulphuric acid
D. Concentrated Acetic acid
marking_schemes.scheme_text: C or Concentrated sulphuric acid or conc. H2SO4
key_points: Concentrated H2SO4 is a dehydrating agent that removes water from cane sugar leaving behind carbon
common_errors: Selecting concentrated Nitric acid
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most candidates answered correctly. A few selected concentrated Nitric acid.

marking_schemes.question_text:
The organic compound having a triple carbon-carbon covalent bond, is:
A. C3H4
B. C3H6
C. C3H8
D. C4H10
marking_schemes.scheme_text: A or C3H4 or propyne or prop-1-yne or 1-propyne
key_points: Alkynes have general formula CnH2n-2; C3H4 fits this formula and contains a triple bond
common_errors: Choosing C3H6 which is an alkene with a double bond
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Well attempted by most candidates, but a few chose C3H6.

marking_schemes.question_text: State one relevant observation for the following reaction: Action of concentrated nitric acid on copper.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Reddish brown or brown or dark brown gas/fumes/vapour is liberated or evolved or released / blue solution/bluish solution formed / a gas with pungent smell is formed which turns potassium iodide paper brown.
key_points: Reddish brown/brown/dark brown gas (NO2) is evolved
If pungent smell mentioned, confirmatory test must follow
marking_schemes.model_answer: Reddish brown gas/fumes are liberated and a blue solution is formed.
accepted_alternatives: Brown gas evolved and blue solution formed
Dark brown fumes released and bluish solution formed
common_errors: Missing the word 'gas'
Writing only 'blue' without the word 'solution'
Not mentioning colour of gas
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Only word 'blue' not accepted. The word 'Solution' is a must. No other colour accepted. A gas with pungent smell should be followed with a confirmatory test.

marking_schemes.question_text: State one relevant observation for the following reaction: Addition of excess ammonium hydroxide into copper sulphate solution.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Inky blue solution / deep blue solution is formed / azure solution / the precipitate or blue precipitate or pale blue precipitate dissolves, or is soluble / the precipitate or blue precipitate or pale blue precipitate (dissolves) forms inky blue/deep blue solution.
key_points: Blue/pale blue precipitate dissolves in excess NH4OH
Inky blue or deep blue solution is formed
marking_schemes.model_answer: A pale blue precipitate is first formed which dissolves in excess ammonium hydroxide to form a deep/inky blue solution.
accepted_alternatives: Blue precipitate dissolves forming deep blue solution
common_errors: Writing 'deep blue precipitate is formed' instead of solution
Not mentioning that precipitate dissolves
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: The word 'Solution' is a must. The word precipitate is not accepted if it is not supported by the word dissolves or soluble.

marking_schemes.question_text: State one relevant observation for the following reaction: A piece of sodium metal is put into ethanol at room temperature.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Bubbles of gas is released / or bubbles seen / effervescence is seen / fizz is formed / colourless gas is released which extinguishes a burning splinter with a pop sound.
key_points: If colourless odourless gas mentioned, confirmatory test must follow
marking_schemes.model_answer: Brisk effervescence is seen; a colourless gas is released which extinguishes a burning splint with a pop sound.
accepted_alternatives: Colourless gas released which burns with a pop sound
common_errors: Stating gas burns with a blue flame instead of extinguishing burning splint with pop sound
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Colourless, odourless gas released should be followed by confirmatory test.

marking_schemes.question_text: State one relevant observation for the following reaction: Zinc carbonate is heated strongly.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: A gas is released which turns lime water milky / a gas is released which has no effect / no change on potassium dichromate solution or potassium permanganate solution or a residue which is yellow when hot and white when cold is formed / white residue is left or formed.
key_points: Gas released turns lime water milky (CO2)
Residue is yellow when hot and white when cold (ZnO)
marking_schemes.model_answer: A gas is released which turns lime water milky, and a residue which is yellow when hot and white when cold is formed.
accepted_alternatives: No effect on potassium dichromate solution
common_errors: Not mentioning the word 'residue'
Writing that residue turns yellow
Not giving confirmatory test for CO2
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Acidified word is not a must but the word solution should be mentioned for potassium dichromate or potassium permanganate.

marking_schemes.question_text: State one relevant observation for the following reaction: Sulphide ore is added to a tank containing oil and water, and then stirred or agitated with air.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Froth / foam is produced / lather is seen / bubbles are seen / ore floats / particles are seen floating / lighter particles float / heavy particles sink / gangue or matrix sink / mud or soil sinks.
marking_schemes.model_answer: Froth is produced and the ore particles float to the surface while the gangue/matrix sinks to the bottom.
common_errors: Explaining froth flotation method instead of observation
Writing that ore mixes with oil and settles down
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Many explained the Froth Flotation method instead of the observation.

marking_schemes.question_text: Write a balanced chemical equation for the following: Reaction of carbon powder and concentrated nitric acid.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: C + 4HNO3 → CO2 + 2H2O + 4NO2
key_points: Correct reactants: C and conc. HNO3
common_errors: Writing CO instead of CO2
Writing NO instead of NO2
Incorrect balancing
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Some candidates did not balance the equations correctly. Some wrote CO instead of CO2, or NO instead of NO2.

marking_schemes.question_text: Write a balanced chemical equation for the following: Reaction of excess ammonia with chlorine.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: 8NH3 + 3Cl2 → 6NH4Cl + N2
common_errors: Writing products as NCl3 and HCl (which is the reaction with excess chlorine)
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Some candidates wrote the products with excess Chlorine as NCl3 and HCl.

marking_schemes.question_text: Write a balanced chemical equation for the following: Reaction of lead nitrate solution with ammonium hydroxide.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Pb(NO3)2 + 2NH4OH → Pb(OH)2 + 2NH4NO3
key_points: Correct formula for lead nitrate: Pb(NO3)2
Correct formula for lead hydroxide: Pb(OH)2
common_errors: Writing incorrect formula for lead hydroxide
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most candidates wrote this correctly. A few wrote the formula of lead hydroxide incorrectly.

marking_schemes.question_text: Write a balanced chemical equation for the following: Producing ethane from bromo ethane using Zn/Cu couple in alcohol.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: C2H5Br + 2[H] →(Zn/Cu couple in alcohol)→ C2H6 + HBr
marking_schemes.model_answer: C2H5Br + 2[H] →(Zn/Cu couple in alcohol)→ C2H6 + HBr
common_errors: Confusion with the condition Zn/Cu couple in alcohol
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Many candidates were confused with the condition given - Zn/Cu couple in alcohol.

marking_schemes.question_text: Write a balanced chemical equation for the following: Complete combustion of ethane.
key_points: Complete combustion produces CO2 and H2O
common_errors: Writing carbon monoxide instead of carbon dioxide as product
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: A few candidates were confused regarding the products and wrote carbon monoxide instead of carbon dioxide.

marking_schemes.question_text: Draw the structural formula for: 2,2 dimethyl pentane
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Structural formula showing a 5-carbon chain with two methyl groups on carbon 2. The methyl branching on the second carbon atom can be from left or right.
key_points: Two methyl groups attached to C2
marking_schemes.model_answer: CH3-C(CH3)2-CH2-CH2-CH3 with full structural formula showing all H atoms
accepted_alternatives: Branching from left or right both accepted
common_errors: Writing condensed formula instead of structural formula
Not understanding branched chain
Showing carbon skeleton without complete structural formula
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Some candidates wrote the condensed formula instead of the structural formula. Many candidates did not understand the difference between straight and branched chain.

marking_schemes.question_text: Draw the structural formula for: methanol
marking_schemes.scheme_text: H-C-O-H with all hydrogen atoms shown on the carbon, or H3C-OH structural formula
key_points: All hydrogen atoms on carbon shown
marking_schemes.model_answer: Full structural formula: H attached to C which is attached to O which is attached to H, with 3 H atoms on C
common_errors: Drawing condensed formula instead of structural formula
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most candidates drew the structural formula correctly. A few candidates drew the condensed formula instead.

marking_schemes.question_text: Draw the structural formula for: Iso propane
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Structural formula showing a central carbon bonded to two CH3 groups and two H atoms (isopropane / 2-methylpropane structure with 3 carbons in branched arrangement)
marking_schemes.model_answer: Full structural formula of isopropane (propane): H3C-CH2-CH3 with all H atoms explicitly shown
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: This part of the question was well attempted by most candidates.

marking_schemes.question_text: Write the IUPAC name for the following compound: acetaldehyde
marking_schemes.scheme_text: ethanal / 1ethanal / ethan-1-al
common_errors: Writing methanal instead of ethanal
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Some candidates wrote the IUPAC name as methanal instead of ethanal.

marking_schemes.question_text: Write the IUPAC name for the following compound: acetylene
marking_schemes.scheme_text: ethyne / 1 ethyne / eth-1-yne
common_errors: Confusion between -ene and -yne suffix
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most candidates attempted well but some were confused between 'ene' and 'yne'.

marking_schemes.question_text: State one relevant reason for the following: Graphite anode is preferred to platinum in the electrolysis of molten lead bromide.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Since graphite anode is unaffected (by the reactive vapours of bromine) or does not react / Platinum is affected by (bromine vapours) or reacts with (bromine vapours).
key_points: Graphite is unaffected by bromine vapours
Platinum reacts with/is affected by bromine vapours
marking_schemes.model_answer: Graphite is unaffected by the reactive vapours of bromine produced during electrolysis, whereas platinum would react with bromine vapours.
accepted_alternatives: Graphite does not react with bromine vapours
Platinum is affected by bromine vapours
common_errors: Stating graphite is cheaper or platinum is expensive
Stating graphite is inert without specifying reason
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Key words were missing in answers. Most candidates mentioned graphite is cheaper or platinum is expensive, instead of stating that graphite remains unaffected by bromine vapour.

marking_schemes.question_text: State one relevant reason for the following: Soda lime is preferred to sodium hydroxide in the laboratory preparation of methane.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Since soda lime is not deliquescent or does not attack glass or sodium hydroxide is deliquescent or CaO is a drying agent or CaO absorbs moisture.
key_points: Soda lime does not attack glass
CaO in soda lime acts as drying agent
marking_schemes.model_answer: Soda lime is not deliquescent and does not attack glass, whereas sodium hydroxide is deliquescent and attacks the glass of the apparatus.
accepted_alternatives: Soda lime does not attack glass
common_errors: Stating soda lime acts as a catalyst
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most candidates mentioned that soda lime acts as a catalyst. Very few candidates gave correct reasoning.

marking_schemes.question_text: State one relevant reason for the following: Hydrated copper sulphate crystals turn white on heating.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: As it loses water of crystallization / loses water / loses definite number of water molecules / turns anhydrous / loses five molecules of water / gets dehydrated.
marking_schemes.model_answer: On heating, hydrated copper sulphate loses its water of crystallization and becomes anhydrous copper sulphate which is white.
common_errors: Not using the term 'water of crystallization'
Writing 'moisture is removed'
Using incorrect term 'Amorphous'
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: The words water of crystallization was missing in most of the answers. Instead candidates wrote moisture is removed.

marking_schemes.question_text: State one relevant reason for the following: Concentrated nitric acid appears yellow, when it is left for a while in a glass bottle.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Concentrated nitric acid itself decomposes to form reddish brown or brown nitrogen dioxide gas which remains dissolved (imparts yellow colour to it) / or NO2 gas formed dissolves in the acid to give (yellow colour).
key_points: NO2 dissolves in acid imparting yellow colour
marking_schemes.model_answer: Concentrated nitric acid decomposes to produce reddish brown nitrogen dioxide (NO2) gas, which dissolves in the acid and imparts a yellow colour to it.
accepted_alternatives: NO2 gas formed dissolves in the acid giving yellow colour
common_errors: Not mentioning that NO2 dissolves in the acid
Simply writing 'due to NO2' without explaining dissolution
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Many candidates did not mention the word 'dissolves' or dissolution of the gas.

marking_schemes.question_text: State one relevant reason for the following: Hydrogen chloride gas fumes in moist air.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: As it is highly soluble in water / high solubility / absorbs moisture and forms mist / affinity for water.
key_points: HCl is highly soluble in water
Absorbs moisture from air to form mist/fumes
marking_schemes.model_answer: Hydrogen chloride gas is highly soluble in water (moisture in air), and absorbs moisture to form tiny droplets of hydrochloric acid, appearing as white fumes/mist.
common_errors: Writing it reacts with ammonia in air
Writing 'dense white fumes are formed' as the reason rather than explanation
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most candidates gave a relevant reason. Some wrote 'because it comes in contact with ammonia gas'.

marking_schemes.question_text: Calculate the amount of each reactant required to produce 750 ml of carbon dioxide, when two volumes of carbon monoxide combine with one volume of oxygen to produce two volumes of carbon dioxide. 2CO + O2 → 2CO2
marking_schemes.scheme_text: 2 mL of carbon monoxide produces 2 ml of carbon dioxide. 750 mL of carbon dioxide requires 750x2/2 = 750 mL of CO. 1 mL of oxygen produces 2ml of carbon dioxide. 750 mL of carbon dioxide requires 750x1/2 = 375 mL of O2. Amount of carbon monoxide required is 750 mL and oxygen is 375 mL.
marking_schemes.model_answer: From 2CO + O2 → 2CO2: To produce 750 mL CO2, CO required = 750 mL and O2 required = 375 mL
common_errors: Calculating volume of oxygen only and missing carbon monoxide
Calculating mass instead of volume
Ignoring the ratio
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Some calculated only the volume of oxygen and missed calculating the volume of carbon monoxide.

marking_schemes.question_text: Calculate the volume occupied by 80 g of carbon dioxide at STP. [Atomic mass of C=12, O=16]
marking_schemes.scheme_text: 44 g of carbon dioxide occupies 22.4 L or 22400 mL. 80 g of carbon dioxide occupies = 80 x 22.4/44 = 40.72 L. Or 80 x 22400/44 = 40720 mL.
marking_schemes.model_answer: Molar mass of CO2 = 44 g. At STP, 44 g CO2 occupies 22.4 L. Therefore, 80 g CO2 occupies = (80 × 22.4)/44 = 40.72 L
common_errors: Incorrect calculation of molecular weight of CO2
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most candidates calculated correctly, but a few made errors in the calculation of M.W of CO2.

marking_schemes.question_text: Calculate the number of molecules in 4.4 gm of CO2. [Atomic mass of C=12, O=16]
key_points: Number of molecules = (4.4/44) x 6.023 x 10^23 = 6.023 x 10^22
marking_schemes.model_answer: Moles of CO2 = 4.4/44 = 0.1 mol. Number of molecules = 0.1 × 6.023 × 10^23 = 6.023 × 10^22 molecules.
common_errors: Calculating number of moles instead of molecules
Not using Avogadro's number
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Many calculated the number of moles instead of molecules. A few did not use Avogadro's number.

marking_schemes.question_text: State the law associated in question no. 1(f)(i) above.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: When gases react, they do so in volumes which bears a simple whole number ratio to one another and to the volumes of the products, if gaseous, provided the temperature and pressure of the reacting gases and their products remain constant.
key_points: Gases react in simple whole number ratio of volumes
Temperature and pressure must remain constant
marking_schemes.model_answer: Gay-Lussac's Law of Combining Volumes: When gases react, they do so in volumes which bear a simple whole number ratio to one another and to the volumes of gaseous products, provided temperature and pressure remain constant.
common_errors: Only naming the law without stating it
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most of the candidates did not state the law. They only named it.

marking_schemes.question_text: Give one word or a phrase for the following statement: The chemical bond formed by a shared pair of electrons, each bonding atom contributing one electron to the pair.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Covalent bond / covalent
key_points: Covalent bond involves sharing of electrons
common_errors: Confusing with coordinate/dative bond
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Several candidates answered correctly, however a few got confused by coordinate bonding.

marking_schemes.question_text: Give one word or a phrase for the following statement: Electrode used as cathode in electrorefining of impure copper.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: pure (thin block) of copper / pure copper
key_points: Cathode in electrorefining is pure copper
marking_schemes.model_answer: Pure copper (thin block of pure copper)
common_errors: Missing the word 'pure'
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: A few candidates missed associating the word 'pure'.

marking_schemes.question_text: Give one word or a phrase for the following statement: The substance prepared by adding other metals to a base metal in appropriate proportions to obtain certain desirable properties.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Alloy
key_points: Alloy is a mixture of metals
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Only a few candidates answered incorrectly.

marking_schemes.question_text: Give one word or a phrase for the following statement: The tendency of an atom to attract electrons to itself when combined in a compound.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: electronegativity / electronegative property
key_points: Electronegativity is the tendency to attract bonding electrons
common_errors: Writing electron affinity instead of electronegativity
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Some candidates wrote electron affinity instead of electronegativity.

marking_schemes.question_text: Give one word or a phrase for the following statement: The reaction in which carboxylic acid reacts with alcohol in the presence of conc. H2SO4 to form a substance having a fruity smell.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: esterification
key_points: Esterification is the reaction between carboxylic acid and alcohol
common_errors: Writing 'ester' or 'neutralization reaction'
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Majority of the candidates gave correct answers. A few mentioned it as 'ester' or neutralization reaction.

marking_schemes.question_text: Fill in the blank: The polar covalent compound in gaseous state that does not conduct electricity is __________. (carbon tetra chloride, ammonia, methane)
marking_schemes.scheme_text: ammonia / NH3
key_points: Ammonia in gaseous state does not conduct electricity
common_errors: Choosing methane instead of ammonia
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most of the candidates answered correctly. Some chose methane instead of ammonia.

marking_schemes.question_text: Fill in the blank: A salt prepared by displacement reaction is __________. (ferric chloride, ferrous chloride, silver chloride)
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Ferrous chloride / FeCl2 / Iron(II) chloride
key_points: Ferrous chloride is prepared by displacement reaction of iron with HCl
Ferric chloride is not by displacement
common_errors: Choosing ferric chloride
Not distinguishing between soluble and insoluble salts
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Some candidates were not able to distinguish between soluble and insoluble salts. A few even chose ferric chloride.

marking_schemes.question_text: Fill in the blank: The number of moles in 11 gm of nitrogen gas is __________. (0.39, 0.49, 0.29) [atomic mass of N=14]
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most of the candidates answered this question correctly.

marking_schemes.question_text: Fill in the blank: An alkali which completely dissociates into ions is __________. (ammonium hydroxide, calcium hydroxide, lithium hydroxide)
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Lithium hydroxide / calcium hydroxide / or Formula accepted
key_points: Lithium hydroxide is a strong alkali
common_errors: Choosing ammonium hydroxide which is a weak alkali
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Many candidates were able to select the correct answer possibly due to the offered options. Very few wrote ammonium hydroxide.

marking_schemes.question_text: Fill in the blank: An alloy used to make statues is__________. (bronze, brass, fuse metal)
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Bronze
key_points: Bronze is used for making statues
common_errors: Choosing Brass
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: This question was attempted correctly by most candidates. A few however chose Brass.

marking_schemes.question_text:
The following table represents the elements and the atomic number.
Element | Atomic number
P | 13
Q | 7
R | 10
Using only the alphabets given in the table, which element combines with hydrogen to form a basic gas?
key_points: Nitrogen combines with hydrogen to form ammonia (NH3) which is a basic gas
marking_schemes.model_answer: Q (element with atomic number 7, which is Nitrogen, forms NH3 - a basic gas)
common_errors: Identifying the element instead of using the given alphabets
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most of the candidates attempted this part correctly. Some candidates identified the elements instead of choosing the given alphabets.
marking_schemes.topic: Periodic Properties and Variations of Properties

marking_schemes.question_text:
The following table represents the elements and the atomic number.
Element | Atomic number
P | 13
Q | 7
R | 10
Using only the alphabets given in the table, which element has an electron affinity zero?
key_points: Noble gases have zero electron affinity as they have complete outer shells
marking_schemes.model_answer: R (element with atomic number 10, which is Neon - a noble gas with zero electron affinity)
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most candidates attempted this correctly.
marking_schemes.topic: Periodic Properties and Variations of Properties

marking_schemes.question_text:
The following table represents the elements and the atomic number.
Element | Atomic number
P | 13
Q | 7
R | 10
Using only the alphabets given in the table, name the element which forms an ionic compound with chlorine.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: P / 13 / Al / Aluminium
key_points: Aluminium forms ionic compound AlCl3 with chlorine
marking_schemes.model_answer: P (element with atomic number 13, which is Aluminium, forms ionic AlCl3 with chlorine)
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most candidates attempted this correctly.

marking_schemes.question_text: Draw the electron dot diagram for Calcium oxide. Represent the electrons by (.) and (x) in the diagram. [Atomic No.: Ca = 20, O = 8]
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Electron dot diagram showing Ca losing 2 electrons (shown with arrows) to O, forming Ca2+ and O2- ions with appropriate charges shown.
key_points: Correct charges on ions: Ca2+ and O2-
Different symbols for electrons from each atom
marking_schemes.model_answer: Ca (with 2 valence electrons as dots) → [Ca]2+ [O with 8 electrons]2-
accepted_alternatives: Both representations with arrow and 2e- notation accepted
common_errors: Not drawing arrows to show transfer
Drawing only one arrow for transfer of two electrons
Not showing charges on ions
Drawing as covalent molecule
Same symbols for electrons from both atoms
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: A number of candidates did not draw arrows to show transfer of electrons. Some drew only one arrow instead of two.

marking_schemes.question_text: Draw the electron dot diagram for Chlorine molecule. Represent the electrons by (.) and (x) in the diagram. [Atomic No.: Cl = 17]
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Electron dot diagram showing two Cl atoms sharing one pair of electrons, with 3 lone pairs on each Cl atom. Different symbols for each atom's electrons.
key_points: One shared pair of electrons between two Cl atoms
Different symbols (. and x) for electrons from each atom
marking_schemes.model_answer: :Cl:Cl: with shared pair shown using different symbols
common_errors: Drawing orbit structure instead of dot diagram
Showing electron pair along with bond
Confusion about number of electrons shared
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Many candidates drew orbit structure or showed the electron pair along with the bond.

marking_schemes.question_text: Draw the electron dot diagram for Water molecule. Represent the electrons by (.) and (x) in the diagram. [Atomic No.: H = 1, O = 8]
marking_schemes.scheme_text: H:O:H with two lone pairs on oxygen shown, and two bonding pairs between H and O atoms using different symbols.
key_points: Different symbols for electrons from each atom
marking_schemes.model_answer: H with (x) sharing with O (.), O having 2 lone pairs, second H with (x) sharing with O
common_errors: Forgetting to draw lone pairs on oxygen
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Some candidates forgot to draw the lone pair of electrons on water.

marking_schemes.question_text:
Choose the correct word which refers to the process of electrolysis from A to E, to match the description: Conducts electricity in aqueous or in molten state.
A: Oxidation B: Cathode C: Anode D: An electrolyte E: Reduction
marking_schemes.scheme_text: D or an electrolyte
key_points: An electrolyte conducts electricity in aqueous or molten state via ions
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most candidates were able to answer this part correctly.

marking_schemes.question_text:
Choose the correct word which refers to the process of electrolysis from A to E, to match the description: Loss of electron takes place at anode.
A: Oxidation B: Cathode C: Anode D: An electrolyte E: Reduction
marking_schemes.scheme_text: A or oxidation
common_errors: Confusing oxidation and reduction
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Some were not able to distinguish between oxidation and reduction reactions.

marking_schemes.question_text:
Choose the correct word which refers to the process of electrolysis from A to E, to match the description: A reducing electrode.
A: Oxidation B: Cathode C: Anode D: An electrolyte E: Reduction
marking_schemes.scheme_text: B or cathode
key_points: Cathode is the reducing electrode where reduction/gain of electrons occurs
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most candidates answered correctly.

marking_schemes.question_text:
Choose the correct word which refers to the process of electrolysis from A to E, to match the description: Electrode connected to the positive end or terminal of the battery.
A: Oxidation B: Cathode C: Anode D: An electrolyte E: Reduction
marking_schemes.scheme_text: C or anode
key_points: Anode is connected to the positive terminal of the battery
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most candidates answered correctly.

marking_schemes.question_text: Baeyer's process is used to concentrate bauxite ore to alumina. Give the balanced chemical equation for the first reaction (bauxite reacting with NaOH) in its conversion from bauxite to alumina.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Al2O3.2H2O + 2NaOH → 2NaAlO2 + 3H2O (at 150-200°C)
key_points: Correct formula for sodium aluminate: NaAlO2
common_errors: Wrong formula for NaAlO2
Unbalanced equation
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most candidates did not write all three equations correctly. Many candidates wrote the wrong formula for NaAlO2.

marking_schemes.question_text: Baeyer's process is used to concentrate bauxite ore to alumina. Give the balanced chemical equation for the second reaction (NaAlO2 reacting with water) in its conversion from bauxite to alumina.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: NaAlO2 + 2H2O → NaOH + Al(OH)3 (at 50-60°C)
common_errors: Incorrect formula for aluminium hydroxide
Not balancing equation
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Many candidates did not write all reactions correctly.

marking_schemes.question_text: Baeyer's process is used to concentrate bauxite ore to alumina. Give the balanced chemical equation for the third reaction (conversion of Al(OH)3 to Al2O3) in its conversion from bauxite to alumina.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: 2Al(OH)3 → Al2O3 + 3H2O (at 1100°C)
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: The third reaction was written correctly by most candidates.

marking_schemes.question_text: Complete the following by selecting the correct option: pH of acetic acid is greater than dilute sulphuric acid. So acetic acid contains __________ concentration of H+ ions. (greater, same, low)
marking_schemes.scheme_text: low or less
key_points: Higher pH means lower H+ concentration
Acetic acid is a weak acid with fewer H+ ions than H2SO4
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most candidates attempted it correctly.

marking_schemes.question_text: Complete the following by selecting the correct option: The indicator which does not change colour on passage of HCl gas is __________. (methyl orange, moist blue litmus, phenolphthalein)
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Phenolphthalein
key_points: Phenolphthalein is colourless in acidic conditions and remains colourless with HCl gas
HCl gas (dry) does not affect phenolphthalein
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: This was attempted correctly by most candidates.

marking_schemes.question_text: Complete the following by selecting the correct option: The acid which cannot act as an oxidizing agent is __________. (conc. H2SO4, conc. HNO3, conc. HCl)
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Concentrated HCl
key_points: Conc. HCl cannot act as an oxidizing agent
Conc. H2SO4 and conc. HNO3 are oxidizing agents
common_errors: Selecting conc. HNO3 due to overlooking the word 'not'
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Many candidates overlooked the word 'not' and instead wrote the oxidizing agent. Majority selected the incorrect option conc. nitric acid.

marking_schemes.question_text:
Match the gas in column I to its identification in column II:
Column I: (i) Hydrogen sulphide
Column II: A. Turns acidified potassium dichromate solution green. B. Turns lime water milky. C. Turns reddish brown when it reacts with oxygen. D. Turns moist lead acetate paper silvery black.
options: A. Turns acidified potassium dichromate solution green
C. Turns reddish brown when it reacts with oxygen
D. Turns moist lead acetate paper silvery black
marking_schemes.scheme_text: D or turns moist lead acetate paper silvery black
key_points: H2S turns moist lead acetate paper silvery black (forms lead sulphide)
marking_schemes.model_answer: D - Turns moist lead acetate paper silvery black
accepted_alternatives: turns moist lead acetate paper silvery black
common_errors: Confusing H2S with SO2 test
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Some wrote that Nitric oxide turns lead acetate paper silvery black.

marking_schemes.question_text:
Match the gas in column I to its identification in column II:
Column I: (ii) Nitric oxide
Column II: A. Turns acidified potassium dichromate solution green. B. Turns lime water milky. C. Turns reddish brown when it reacts with oxygen. D. Turns moist lead acetate paper silvery black.
options: A. Turns acidified potassium dichromate solution green
C. Turns reddish brown when it reacts with oxygen
D. Turns moist lead acetate paper silvery black
marking_schemes.scheme_text: C or turns reddish brown when it reacts with oxygen
key_points: NO turns reddish brown when it reacts with oxygen to form NO2
marking_schemes.model_answer: C - Turns reddish brown when it reacts with oxygen
accepted_alternatives: turns reddish brown when it reacts with oxygen
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most candidates answered correctly.

marking_schemes.question_text:
Match the gas in column I to its identification in column II:
Column I: (iii) Carbon dioxide
Column II: A. Turns acidified potassium dichromate solution green. B. Turns lime water milky. C. Turns reddish brown when it reacts with oxygen. D. Turns moist lead acetate paper silvery black.
options: A. Turns acidified potassium dichromate solution green
C. Turns reddish brown when it reacts with oxygen
D. Turns moist lead acetate paper silvery black
marking_schemes.scheme_text: B or turns lime water milky
key_points: CO2 turns lime water milky by forming CaCO3
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most candidates answered correctly.

marking_schemes.question_text:
Match the gas in column I to its identification in column II:
Column I: (iv) Sulphur dioxide
Column II: A. Turns acidified potassium dichromate solution green. B. Turns lime water milky. C. Turns reddish brown when it reacts with oxygen. D. Turns moist lead acetate paper silvery black.
options: A. Turns acidified potassium dichromate solution green
C. Turns reddish brown when it reacts with oxygen
D. Turns moist lead acetate paper silvery black
marking_schemes.scheme_text: A or turns acidified potassium dichromate solution green / B or turns lime water milky or A and B
key_points: SO2 turns acidified potassium dichromate solution green (reduces it)
SO2 also turns lime water milky
marking_schemes.model_answer: A - Turns acidified potassium dichromate solution green
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Both A and B accepted for sulphur dioxide.

marking_schemes.question_text: Differentiate between Conductor and Electrolyte based on conducting particles.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Conductor – conduction due to electrons. Electrolyte – conduction due to ions.
key_points: Electrolytes conduct via ions (in aqueous or molten state)
marking_schemes.model_answer: Conductor conducts electricity due to free electrons, while an electrolyte conducts electricity due to ions.
common_errors: Writing atoms instead of ions
Not basing answer on conducting particles as specified
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Many candidates could not answer this part correctly. The differences were not based on the specified parameters. Some wrote atoms in place of ions.

marking_schemes.question_text: Differentiate between Cations and Anions based on formation from an atom.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Cations are formed by the loss of electrons from an atom / or oxidation of an atom / donating electrons. Anions are formed by the gain of electrons by an atom / reduction of an atom / accepting electrons.
key_points: Cations: formed by loss of electrons (oxidation)
Anions: formed by gain of electrons (reduction)
marking_schemes.model_answer: Cations are formed when an atom loses electrons (oxidation). Anions are formed when an atom gains electrons (reduction).
accepted_alternatives: Cations: donating electrons; Anions: accepting electrons
common_errors: Stating cations migrate to cathode and anions to anode (which is behaviour, not formation)
Stating cations gain electrons and anions lose electrons (reversed)
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most candidates wrote cations migrate towards cathode and anions towards anode instead of describing formation.

marking_schemes.question_text: Differentiate between Acid and Alkali based on formation of type of ions.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Acid – forms H+ ions or hydronium (ions in solution) or H3O+ or hydrogen ions. Alkali – forms hydroxyl (ion) or OH– (in solution) or hydroxide ion/hydroxide.
key_points: Acid forms H+ / H3O+ ions in solution
Alkali forms OH- ions in solution
marking_schemes.model_answer: An acid forms H+ (hydronium) ions in aqueous solution, while an alkali forms OH- (hydroxide) ions in solution.
accepted_alternatives: Acid: H3O+ ions; Alkali: hydroxide ions
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Answered correctly by majority of the candidates.

marking_schemes.question_text: Draw the structures of isomers of pentane: pentane (straight chain isomer)
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Structural formula of n-pentane: H-C-C-C-C-C-H with all H atoms shown (5 carbon straight chain)
marking_schemes.model_answer: n-pentane: CH3-CH2-CH2-CH2-CH3 shown as full structural formula
common_errors: Missing H atoms
Incorrect carbon count
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most candidates drew the first isomer correctly but could not draw the other two isomers.

marking_schemes.question_text: Draw the structures of isomers of pentane: 2-methylbutane (branched chain isomer)
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Structural formula of 2-methylbutane: 4-carbon chain with a CH3 branch on C2, all H atoms shown.
marking_schemes.model_answer: 2-methylbutane: CH3-CH(CH3)-CH2-CH3 shown as full structural formula
common_errors: Not drawing branched structure correctly
Missing H atoms
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Branched structures were not drawn correctly. Many candidates did not understand the difference between straight and branched chain.

marking_schemes.question_text: Draw the structures of isomers of pentane: 2,2-dimethylpropane (branched chain isomer)
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Structural formula of 2,2-dimethylpropane: central carbon with 4 CH3 groups, all H atoms shown.
marking_schemes.model_answer: 2,2-dimethylpropane: C(CH3)4 shown as full structural formula with central carbon bonded to 4 CH3 groups
common_errors: Not drawing all three isomers
Incorrect branching
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Some candidates drew only two isomers.

marking_schemes.question_text: Hydrogen chloride gas is prepared in the laboratory using concentrated sulphuric acid and sodium chloride. Give the balanced chemical equation for the reaction with suitable condition(s) if any.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: NaCl + (conc.) H2SO4 →(less than 200°C)→ NaHSO4 + HCl
key_points: Correct reactants: NaCl and conc. H2SO4
common_errors: Not mentioning condition
Using greater than sign instead of less than sign for temperature
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Several candidates did not mention the condition or wrote incorrect condition. Some used greater than sign instead of less than sign.

marking_schemes.question_text: Hydrogen chloride gas is prepared in the laboratory using concentrated sulphuric acid and sodium chloride. Why is concentrated sulphuric acid used instead of concentrated nitric acid?
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Concentrated H2SO4 is non-volatile / least volatile / less volatile / has high boiling point (and hence can displace the more volatile HCl gas from the salt). OR Concentrated nitric acid is a volatile acid / low boiling point and (will displace out itself along with HCl gas).
key_points: H2SO4 is non-volatile/has high boiling point
HNO3 is volatile/has low boiling point and would escape with HCl
marking_schemes.model_answer: Concentrated H2SO4 is non-volatile (has a very high boiling point) and can displace the more volatile HCl gas from the salt. Concentrated HNO3 is volatile and would escape along with HCl gas.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Almost all attempted correctly.

marking_schemes.question_text: Hydrogen chloride gas is prepared in the laboratory using concentrated sulphuric acid and sodium chloride. How is the gas collected?
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Upward displacement of air / downward delivery / downward delivery of gas
key_points: HCl is denser than air so collected by upward displacement of air (downward delivery)
marking_schemes.model_answer: By upward displacement of air (downward delivery), since HCl gas is denser than air.
common_errors: Stating it is collected by downward displacement of air (incorrect)
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Some candidates wrote that the gas was collected by downward displacement of air.

marking_schemes.question_text: Hydrogen chloride gas is prepared in the laboratory using concentrated sulphuric acid and sodium chloride. Name the drying agent not used for drying the gas.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Quick lime / calcium oxide / phosphorus pentoxide
key_points: CaO (quick lime) cannot be used as it is alkaline and reacts with HCl
P2O5 cannot be used as it reacts with HCl
marking_schemes.model_answer: Quick lime (CaO) or phosphorus pentoxide (P2O5) — these cannot be used as they react with HCl gas.
common_errors: Missing the word 'not used' and identifying the drying agent as conc. H2SO4
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Some candidates missed out the word 'not used', hence, identified the drying agent as Conc. H2SO4 instead of CaO and P2O5.

marking_schemes.question_text: Distinguish between Calcium nitrate and Zinc nitrate solution using a reagent as a chemical test.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Add NaOH/KOH/dil H2SO4 to both the solutions. Calcium nitrate forms a white precipitate which is insoluble in excess of NaOH while Zinc nitrate forms a gelatinous white precipitate soluble in excess. With (dilute) Sulphuric acid: Calcium nitrate forms a white precipitate while Zinc nitrate does not form precipitate. Or With NH4OH: Calcium nitrate no reaction or no precipitate while with Zinc nitrate it forms a (gelatinous white) precipitate soluble in excess.
key_points: Difference in solubility of precipitate in excess reagent
marking_schemes.model_answer: Add NaOH to both solutions. Calcium nitrate gives a white precipitate insoluble in excess NaOH, while zinc nitrate gives a gelatinous white precipitate which dissolves in excess NaOH.
accepted_alternatives: Using dil H2SO4: Ca(NO3)2 gives white precipitate, Zn(NO3)2 does not
Using NH4OH: no reaction with Ca(NO3)2; white gelatinous precipitate with Zn(NO3)2 soluble in excess
common_errors: Wrong reagent chosen
Not mentioning observations for both substances
Stating observations without mentioning the reagent
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: A number of candidates chose the incorrect reagent; others could not write the correct observations.

marking_schemes.question_text: Distinguish between Ammonium sulphate crystals and Sodium sulphate crystals using a reagent as a chemical test.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Add any alkali/base. Ammonium sulphate produces a pungent colourless gas or colourless gas is released which turns red litmus blue. While there is no reaction with sodium sulphate. Or no pungent gas released.
key_points: Ammonium sulphate: pungent colourless gas (NH3) turns red litmus blue
Sodium sulphate: no reaction/no pungent gas
marking_schemes.model_answer: Add NaOH to both. Ammonium sulphate produces a pungent colourless gas (ammonia) which turns red litmus blue. Sodium sulphate shows no reaction.
common_errors: Not stating observations for both compounds
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Majority distinguished using different chemical reagents; at times, the observations were not correct.

marking_schemes.question_text: Distinguish between Magnesium chloride and Magnesium nitrate solution using a reagent as a chemical test.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Add silver nitrate/lead nitrate solution to both / or perform brown ring test for nitrates. Magnesium chloride forms a white precipitate while there is no reaction with magnesium nitrate. Or Magnesium chloride does not form brown ring with Brown ring test while magnesium nitrate forms a brown ring.
key_points: Reagent: AgNO3 or lead nitrate or brown ring test
MgCl2: white precipitate (AgCl) with AgNO3; no brown ring
Mg(NO3)2: no precipitate with AgNO3; forms brown ring
marking_schemes.model_answer: Add AgNO3 solution to both. Magnesium chloride forms a white precipitate (AgCl), while magnesium nitrate shows no reaction.
accepted_alternatives: Brown ring test: MgCl2 no brown ring; Mg(NO3)2 forms brown ring
Lead nitrate also accepted as reagent
common_errors: Not mentioning the reagent
Stating observations without correct chemical test
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Several wrote the correct observation without mentioning the reagent.

marking_schemes.question_text: Calculate the percentage of Fluorine in sodium aluminium fluoride [Na3AlF6]. [Atomic Mass: Na = 23, Al= 27, F= 19]
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Molecular weight of Na3AlF6 = 23x3 + 27 + 19x6 = 210. Percentage of F = 114 x 100 / 210 = 54.28% or 54.2% or 54%
common_errors: Incorrect calculation of molecular weight of Na3AlF6
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Almost all the candidates answered this part correctly. A few calculated the molecular weight incorrectly.

marking_schemes.question_text: Calculate the percentage of Sodium in sodium aluminium fluoride [Na3AlF6]. [Atomic Mass: Na = 23, Al= 27, F= 19]
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Percentage of Na = 69x100/210 = 32.85% or 32.8% or 33%
common_errors: Using 23 instead of 69 (3×23) for sodium mass
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most candidates did this correctly. Some calculated the percentage with only 23 instead of 3×23.

marking_schemes.question_text: Calculate the percentage of Aluminium in sodium aluminium fluoride [Na3AlF6]. [Atomic Mass: Na = 23, Al= 27, F= 19]
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Percentage of Al = 27 x 100 / 210 = 12.85% or 12.8% or 13%
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Almost all candidates attempted this subpart correctly.

marking_schemes.question_text: State the volume occupied by 40 gm of methane at STP, if its vapour density (V.D.) is 8.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: RMM = 2 x VD = 2 x 8 = 16 g/mol. 16 g of CH4 occupy 22.4 L at STP. Therefore 40 g of CH4 occupy = 22.4 x 40/16 = 56 L or 56000 mL.
common_errors: Using VD = 8 directly as molar mass instead of calculating RMM = 2 × VD = 16
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Several candidates did the calculation taking the value of vapour density as '8', instead of calculating RMM = 2 x VD = 16.

marking_schemes.question_text: Calculate the number of moles present in 160 gm of NaOH. [Atomic Mass: Na = 23, H= 1, O= 16]
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Number of moles of NaOH = weight in grams / molecular weight = 160 / 40 = 4 moles
marking_schemes.model_answer: Molar mass of NaOH = 23 + 16 + 1 = 40 g/mol. Number of moles = 160/40 = 4 moles
common_errors: Incorrect molecular weight of NaOH
Calculating molecules instead of moles
Incorrect substitution in formula
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Some candidates calculated molecular weight of NaOH incorrectly. A large number made incorrect substitution.

marking_schemes.question_text: Identify salt P from the following observations: Salt P has light bluish green colour. On heating, it produces a black coloured residue. Salt P produces brisk effervescence with dil. HCl and the gas evolved turns lime water milky, but no action with acidified potassium dichromate solution.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: CuCO3 or copper carbonate or copper(II) carbonate
key_points: Light bluish green colour indicates copper salt
Effervescence with HCl, gas turns lime water milky = CO2 (carbonate)
No action with KMnO4/K2Cr2O7 rules out sulphite
common_errors: Identifying as calcium carbonate instead of copper carbonate
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Few candidates made errors in identifying the salt. Some identified it as calcium carbonate instead of copper carbonate.

marking_schemes.question_text: Identify salt Q from the following observations: Salt Q is white in colour. On strong heating, it produces buff yellow residue and liberates reddish brown gas. Solution of salt Q produces chalky white insoluble precipitate with excess of ammonium hydroxide.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Pb(NO3)2 or lead nitrate or lead(II) nitrate
key_points: Buff yellow residue on heating = PbO
White precipitate insoluble in excess NH4OH indicates lead (Pb2+)
common_errors: Identifying as zinc nitrate
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Some candidates were confused and identified the salt as zinc nitrate.

marking_schemes.question_text: Identify salt R from the following observations: Salt R is black in colour. On reacting with concentrated HCl, it liberates a pungent greenish yellow gas which turns moist starch iodide paper blue black.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: MnO2 or manganese dioxide or manganese(IV) oxide
key_points: Reaction with conc. HCl to give greenish yellow gas (Cl2)
Cl2 turns moist starch iodide paper blue black
common_errors: Identifying as Copper oxide (CuO) which is also black
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Several candidates mistook the black compound to be Copper oxide.

marking_schemes.question_text: Identify the substance underlined: The electrode that increases in mass during the electro-refining of silver.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: cathode or negative electrode or reducing electrode or pure silver or pure silver strip or pure silver metal or pure Ag
key_points: Cathode increases in mass during electrorefining
Pure silver is deposited at cathode
common_errors: Giving anode instead of cathode
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Many candidates gave incorrect answers and mentioned anode instead of cathode.

marking_schemes.question_text: Identify the substance underlined: The acid that is a dehydrating as well as a drying agent.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: concentrated sulphuric acid or conc. H2SO4
key_points: Concentrated H2SO4 acts as both dehydrating and drying agent
common_errors: Omitting the word 'concentrated'
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: The word concentrated was missing in some cases.

marking_schemes.question_text: Identify the substance underlined: The catalyst used to oxidize ammonia into nitric oxide.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Platinum or Pt or Cu (copper) or Ni (Nickel) or Rh (Rhodium)
key_points: Platinum (or other metals like Cu, Ni, Rh) is used as catalyst in catalytic oxidation of NH3 to NO
common_errors: Writing Fe instead of platinum
Writing V2O5 (used in Contact process for SO3)
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Some candidates wrote Fe instead of platinum. A few mentioned V2O5.

marking_schemes.question_text: Copy and complete the following paragraph using the options given in brackets: Alkenes are a homologous series of (i) __________ (saturated / unsaturated) hydrocarbons.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Unsaturated
key_points: Alkenes contain double bonds and are unsaturated
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most candidates answered correctly.

marking_schemes.question_text: Copy and complete the following paragraph using the options given in brackets: Alkenes are characterized by the general formula (ii) __________ (CnH2n+2 / CnH2n).
marking_schemes.scheme_text: CnH2n
key_points: General formula for alkenes is CnH2n
common_errors: Writing CnH2n+2 which is for alkanes
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: A few got confused and wrote CnH2n+2.

marking_schemes.question_text: Copy and complete the following paragraph using the options given in brackets: Alkenes undergo (iii) __________ (addition / substitution) reactions.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Addition
key_points: Alkenes undergo addition reactions due to the presence of double bond
common_errors: Writing substitution (which is for alkanes)
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: A few got confused and wrote substitution.

marking_schemes.question_text: Copy and complete the following paragraph using the options given in brackets: Alkenes also undergo (iv) ________ (hydrogenation / dehydrogenation) to form alkanes.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Hydrogenation
key_points: Hydrogenation of alkenes (addition of H2) converts them to alkanes
common_errors: Writing dehydrogenation
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: A few got confused and wrote dehydrogenation.

marking_schemes.question_text: Write balanced chemical equations for the preparation of Copper sulphate using Method A: Neutralization.
marking_schemes.scheme_text:
CuO + H2SO4 → CuSO4 + H2O
Or Cu(OH)2 + H2SO4 → CuSO4 + 2H2O
Or CuCO3 + H2SO4 → CuSO4 + H2O + CO2
Or Cu(HCO3)2 + H2SO4 → CuSO4 + 2H2O + 2CO2
common_errors: Using copper sulphate as reactant
Using sodium sulphate instead of sulphuric acid
Incorrect reactants selected
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most candidates matched the salt with the method instead of writing equations. Reactants selected were incorrect in some cases.

marking_schemes.question_text: Write balanced chemical equations for the preparation of Zinc carbonate using Method B: Precipitation.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: ZnCl2 + Na2CO3 → ZnCO3 + 2NaCl (or any soluble salts of zinc along with carbonates of sodium, potassium or ammonium as reactants)
key_points: Precipitation: two soluble salts reacting to form insoluble ZnCO3
Correct soluble zinc salt as reactant
Carbonate of Na, K or NH4 as other reactant
common_errors: Using carbonic acid as reactant
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Some candidates took carbonic acid as one of the reactants.

marking_schemes.question_text: Write balanced chemical equations for the preparation of Ammonium sulphate using Method C: Titration.
marking_schemes.scheme_text:
2NH4OH + H2SO4 → (NH4)2SO4 + 2H2O
Or 2NH3 + H2SO4 → (NH4)2SO4
key_points: Titration used for soluble salts with soluble bases
common_errors: Incorrect reactants
Incorrect formula for ammonium sulphate
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Either the reactants selected were incorrect, or formula of ammonium sulphate written was incorrect in some cases.

marking_schemes.question_text: Name the following element: An alkaline earth metal present in group 2 and period 3.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Magnesium or Mg
common_errors: Writing an element from period 2 and group 3
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most candidates attempted this correctly, but some wrote one element of period 2 and another element from group 3.
marking_schemes.topic: Periodic Properties and Variations of Properties

marking_schemes.question_text: Name the following element: A trivalent metal used to make light tools.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Aluminium or Al
key_points: Aluminium is used to make light tools due to low density
common_errors: Not relating trivalent to aluminium
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Some candidates could not relate the term trivalent metal and made errors.

marking_schemes.question_text: Name the following element: A monovalent non-metal present in fluorspar.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Fluorine or F
key_points: Fluorine (F) is the monovalent non-metal present in fluorspar
common_errors: Naming calcium (which is in fluorspar but is a metal, not non-metal)
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Some candidates named calcium as they might have missed out on the word non-metal.
marking_schemes.topic: Periodic Properties and Variations of Properties

marking_schemes.question_text: An aqueous solution of nickel (II) sulphate was electrolyzed using nickel electrodes. What do you observe at the cathode and anode respectively?
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Cathode – silvery metal deposited or coated or sticks / nickel or metal is deposited or coated or sticks / silvery deposit / increases in size or mass. Anode – Size decreases / reduction in mass / Anode dissolves / Anode Diminishes / Anode loses weight.
marking_schemes.model_answer: At cathode: silvery nickel metal is deposited, increasing its mass. At anode: the nickel electrode dissolves/decreases in size and mass.
accepted_alternatives: Cathode: increases in size/mass; Anode: diminishes/loses weight
common_errors: Associating cathode and anode observations in reverse
Writing electrode reactions instead of observations
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Many candidates could not give the correct observation at the cathode/anode. Some wrote cathode and anode reactions instead of observations.

marking_schemes.question_text: An aqueous solution of nickel (II) sulphate was electrolyzed using nickel electrodes. Name the cation that remains as a spectator ion in the solution.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Hydrogen ion or H+ or hydrogen
key_points: H+ ions from water do not get discharged when Ni2+ is present and active electrode is used
common_errors: Listing all possible ions as spectator ions
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Several candidates were not able to identify the spectator ions - all possible ions were mentioned.

marking_schemes.question_text:
An aqueous solution of nickel (II) sulphate was electrolyzed using nickel electrodes. Which equation for the reaction at the anode is correct?
1. Ni → Ni2+ + 2e–
2. Ni + 2e– → Ni2+
3. Ni2+ → Ni + 2e–
4. Ni2+ + 2e– → Ni
marking_schemes.scheme_text: 1 or Ni → Ni2+ + 2e– Or Ni - 2e- → Ni2+
common_errors: Selecting incorrect options; majority selected wrong option
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Majority of the candidates selected an incorrect option.
